title: Pour Forth the Oil, — Pour Boldly Forth
description: Pour Forth the Oil, — Pour Boldly Forth in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Richard Chenevix Trench wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 294, “The Law of Love. 2 Kings, iv. 3”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Pour forth the oil, pour bold-ly forth; It will not fail, un-til Thou fai-lest ves-sels to pro-vide Which it may large-ly fill.

lines: Pour forth the oil, — pour boldly forth;
Make channels for the streams of love,
But if at any time we cease
The very founts of love for us
Will soon be parched and dried.
For we must share, if we would keep
Ceasing to give, we cease to have; —
Such is the law of love.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Richard Chenevix Trench died in 1886.
credits: Words by Richard Chenevix Trench (1807–1886), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
